newsitem.title: RUSSIA: 24 journalists killed in CIS this year.
newsitem.headline: 24 journalists killed in CIS this year.

text.p: Twenty four journalists were killed in Russia and the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) this year, bringing the toll to 130 since the Soviet Union fell apart, a human rights official said on Wednesday.
Oleg Panfilov, of the Glasnost Defence Fund that monitors human rights in the former Soviet Union, told Reuters that they were print, television and radio journalists.
"In Russia, the situation is still bad," he said, adding that 19 of the journalists had been killed in Russia itself.
Many reporters, both Russian and foreign, have been killed in the breakaway region of Chechnya, where Russian troops spent 21 months trying to crush an independence bid.
Panfilov said journalists' rights were most at risk in Azerbaijan, Belarus, Moldova and Kazakhstan.
He was especially worried about the situation in Belarus, where hardline President Alexander Lukashenko has cracked down on reporters thought to be backing the opposition.
The fund was named after the openness campaign of Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev before the collapse of the Soviet Union at the end of 1991.

The CIS, set up by Russian President Boris Yeltsin and his Ukrainian and Belarussian counterparts in December 1991, comprises 12 of the 15 former Soviet republics. The three Baltic states of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania refused to join.
